Evidence-budget replay

One shared allocation policy offers the first five whole originals in module round-robin order, with a 9,000-byte serialized evidence limit. No source is truncated or replaced using reference labels. These are case-level budget simulations; no judgment model was called. This table follows the cohort filter and retains every requested module of each case.

Protocol, failures and audit

There are 40 authored scenario families with five correlated variants among the new 200 notes. These are development stress inputs, not 200 independent patients. Untagged legacy notes request all five disease modules. Modules without existing source labels are retained for execution checks and omitted from recall denominators.

Two initial adapter integration errors were repaired in a separate child run: source graph mapping and prefix baseline status/module. All 714 original failures remain in the parent journal. The unchanged strategies were rerun with their recorded actual embedding responses; no reference backfill, simulated graph backend or model-generated guideline text was used.

The first LightRAG execution had 363 observations for 357 queries because two controllers overlapped. Its complete invalid batch, including all failures and repeated observations, is retained. Primary LightRAG metrics use a fresh exclusive serial run of all 357 queries with unchanged settings and no answer-based selection.

This comparison makes no fitness-judgment calls. Source retrieval, accepted citation identifiers and supported clinical reasoning are distinct measurements.
